en: The Chapter on Similes, Section on the Ants.
2. The Question of the Cat’s Limbs “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘two limbs of a cat should be adopted,’ which are those two limbs that should be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, a cat—whether it has gone into a cave, or into a hollow tree, or into the interior of a house—seeks only for a mouse;”

In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga who is devoted to yoga—whether he has gone to a village, or to the forest, or to the foot of a tree, or to an empty hut—should, being constantly and continuously heedful, seek only the food that is mindfulness directed to the body.
This, Great King, is the first quality of the cat that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, a cat seeks its prey only within its own domain.
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner, a follower of yoga, should dwell observing the arising and passing away within these very five aggregates of clinging:
"Such is form, such its origin, such its passing away;
such is feeling, such its origin, such its passing away; such is perception, such its origin..."
‘Such are formations, such is the arising of formations, such is the passing away of formations;
such is consciousness, such is the arising of consciousness, such is the passing away of consciousness.
This, Great King, is the second quality of the cat that should be adopted.
This was also spoken, O Great King, by the Blessed One, the God above gods:
“One need not go far from here;
what will the pinnacle of existence do?”
find it within your own body.
This is the second question, concerning the cat’s eye.
